newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bond spreads mixed, curve steepens.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bond spreads mixed, curve steepens.

text.p: Australian bond spreads finished mixed, and the yield curve steepened, on a day dominated by the release of the government's mid-year budget review.
Bond spreads opened wider as the local market caught up with two days of offshore weakness following a local holiday weekend.
The weakening market saw the futures curve test down towards 90 points, near its lowest level this year.
Through the morning trade was fairly quiet as bonds were focusing on the U.S. employment cost index later today and Wednesday's local December quarter inflation data.
U.S. wage inflation data is expected to determine market sentiment on the likelihood of a U.S. rate rise following next week's FOMC meeting. A strong rise will be bearish for bonds.

Local bonds have held up reasonbably well in a time of rising yields. Spreads to U.S. Treasuries have held near three year lows over the past week amid the bearishness in U.S. markets, where the 30-year Treasury rose last night to its highest level since late September.
The release of the government's mid year budget review was mixed for the bond market.

The news of lower inflation forecasts and a higher unemployment forecast was positive for the short end, while the unchanged growth forecast and the larger budget deficit weighed on the longer part of the curve.
As a result, the short end strengthened most on late buying into the close, with the futures curve moving decisively above the 92 point support level.

As the inflation and the unemployment revisions, combined with Wednesday's inflation data, are expected to remain supportive of those pushing for another rate cut, it is possible the short end could continue its local outperformance, traders said.
